rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE DEATH PENALTY REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7659, ENTITLED, `AN ACT TO IMPOSE THE DEATH PENALTY ON CERTAIN HEINOUS CRIMES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED, OTHER SPECIAL PENAL LAWS, ANDFOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: The death penalty is hereby abolished and in lieu thereof, the penalty of reclusion perpetua shall be imposed. Rationale: In this light, it is about time we rethink our alternatives and act not out of fear but adbance from a genuine understanding ofthe situation. Let us finally realize that justice must likewise be tempered with mercy in order for genuine repentance and change to have a chance to propser. Hence, emphasis must be placed on restorative justice rather than reributive justice. Fallen characters should best be molded and not merely stripped of their humanity by banishing and condemning them to death.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05114

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT ALL CONTRACTUAL AND CASUAL EMPLOYEES IN THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE BE PAID THEIR CORRESPONDING WAGES DURING SPECIAL PUBLIC HOLIDAYS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Raionale: All contractual and casual employees work under the principle of "no work, no pay." During non-working special public holidays when tenured employees are paid a full day's wage, said "marginalized" employees do not enjoy the same privilege. This situation may very well be seen as unfair, considering that they too are burdened by the same problems confronting the regular employees such as the rising cost of living, basic health care and decent education for their children. This practice runs counter to the government's declared policy aforementioned, and aggravates the already impoverished state of most Filipino families.

rows.abstract: The state of public health in the Philippines may have improved in the past decade due to the allocations given by government in promoting public health services. No. 6657 or the Comrehensive Agrarian Reform Law (CARL) by removing salt beds from the list of private lands that can be taken over for purposes of agrarian reform, in order to ensure adequate areas for sal production; (2) Iodized Salt manufacturers and Iodized salt importersshall be exempt from paying the Value Added Tax (VAT) on iodized salt, in order to encourage the continuous availability of iodized salt for human and animal consumption; and (3) Importers of iodizing equipment and iodides shall be granted exemptionfrom customs duties.

In spite of the sanitation requirements for such places, accidents still do happen and in fact emergency case of people getting suddenly sick in such areas occur and in most cases, there are no first-aid stations or clinics to go for such unfortunate ill-stricken people.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND ARTICLE ONE THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED AND TWENTY-THREE OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THREE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-SIX, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed amendment of Article 1723 of the Civil Code of the Philippines aims to strengthen the liability for damages if a building collapses and it includes damages to any infrastucture project which require a major or complete repair within a period of fifteen (15) years from the sate of completion of the building or infrastructure project.> Presently, Article 1723 of said Civil Code covers only building structures and does not include other infrastructure projects such as bridges, fly-over, roads, airports and the like. The proposed bill seeks to expand the coverage of this provisions (Article 1723) by including therein all infrastructure orojects for the purpose of determining responsibility and accountability of the engineer and arrchitect, as well as the contractors or subcontractors arising from non-observance of proper design or specifications or by reason of the use of poor and substandard materials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2002-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE INCLUSION IN THE CURRICULA OF MEDICINE, DENTISTRY, NURSING, MIDWIFERY AND OTHER ALLIED MEDICAL COURSES OF A SUBJECT ON THE PRIMARY-HEALTH- CARE- APPROACH, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Primarily-healt h-care-approach is the preventive-cura tive process pursued in health development, which is community-based , accessible, acceptable, interrelated with supportive socio-economic development, and sustainable at a cost affordable to the government and community.> All schools offering degrees in medicine, dentistry, nursing,midwife ry and other allied medical professions shall integrate in the curricula for these courses, a primary-health- care-approach subject. In support of this,the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) shall make adjustments, provide incentives and set accreditation criteria that would ensure an equitable distribution of stundets enrolled in medicine and the other allied courses from the different regionsof the country.

rows.abstract: All beach resort owners/maintain ers accredited by the Department of Tourism (DOT) shall, before a permit can be issued by a local government unit, construct and maintain waterworks and sewerage system that will provide potable water to the public and ensure the proper disposal of waster materials therein. In addition, beach resot owners are rerquired to maintain sanitary comfort rooms, first aid and lifeguard facilities and other amenities.> Any beach resort owner or maintainer who fails to comply with this Act within one hundred twenty (12) days after the approval thereof, shall upon conviction, be penalized by a fine of not less than Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) nor more than One Hundred Thousand Pesos (P100,000.00) without prejudiice to the suspension of his license to operate the resort until compliance thereof.

rows.author: D013
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICS EDUCATION FUND, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Science and mathematics are two important subjects Filipino students must study and if possible, excel in; not only to lodge the Philippines at the helm of global competition in these fields but also for their own personal advancement ascitizens of this country.> This bill seeks to provide for funds to support activities and projects that will assist Filipino students to improve on their science and mathematics skills. The fund will establish a research, development and training trust fund for research, curriculum development and teacher taining in science and mathematics, to be administered and managed by the National Institute for Science and Mathematics Education Development (NISMED) of the University of the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2002-07-30
